page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests which fall into the bottom 10% to 25% categories. However, multi-core execution scales effectively to average levels, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores all placing in the middle 50% tier. Memory bandwidth remains stable at average levels, reaching 75.3 GB/sec for uncached large block reads and 53.85 GB/sec for uncached writes.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.se1ne.4xlarge offers a dense memory allocation relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require top-tier single-threaded CPU speeds. The lack of bundled local storage means storage costs are externalized to network volumes. This hardware profile is well-suited for relational databases, Redis caching layers, multi-threaded text and image processing, and moderate web serving workloads.
